surface_mechanism_description: The surface periodicity of both the Cd- and Te-stabilized surfaces does not change with substrate temperature. The observed surface periodicity reflects mainly the dimerization of surface atoms, which also occurs at submonolayer coverages. The intensity of the Cd spot is a direct measure of the Cd surface coverage, and the intensity of the Te spot is a direct measure of the Te coverage. During Cd deposition, the intensity of the Cd spot increases linearly with time up to a saturation value, while during Te deposition, the Te spot intensity increases but not proportionally to the offered Te flux.
evidence: During Cd deposition, the intensity of the Cd spot increases linearly with time up to a saturation value. The two curves correspond within the experimental error of the beam flux calibration (~ ± 5%). So we conclude that the intensity of the Cd spot is a direct measure of the Cd surface coverage. As soon as a surface coverage of one monolayer is reached, the intensity saturates. During Te deposition, the Te spot intensity increases, but not proportional to the offered Te flux. The dashed line marked 'model 2' in fig. 2 represents the calculated Te coverage with the actual Te flux of 0.16 monolayers/s according to this model. Again the correspondence between the intensity of the spot and the simple model is very good, although an exact fit would correspond to j = 0.2 monolayers/s. In analogy to the Cd spot, we think that the intensity of the Te spot is a direct measure for the Te coverage of the surface.
